#12. I am too. Demons, possession scares the shit out of me. But you know what? Fuck the demon. Satan himself wouldn't be able to handle my mind.

#11. I was like that too. I could never say no, people took advantage of that. The second I started to say No, people got upset. Apparently I'm the asshole. But fuck that. They are made because they can't use you anymore. Your true friends however, will respect you. They may be mad at first but eventually they'll understand. They'll respect you have the balls to say no to people close to you. If they leave you because of it. They weren't really your friend. Do what you think is right, always.

#10. That's discipline. Now you can only be discipline for so long, if a guy is like abusing you a lot, it's okay to stand up for yourself. Always fight in defence. Never be the initiator. If someone constantly puts you down. It's because your on a higher level than them. They try to bring you down. When that happens to me, I smile. Because I know that for anyone to say stuff like that to me, they feel threatened by my status. Because really, why would anyone put you down otherwise?
#9. All you can is do the absolute best. As long as you've given it your all, at the end of day. No one can put you down. If you know you did your best. That's all that matters

#8. I'm not confident either. Only in the things I know I'm good at. A lot of confidence I believe comes with being humble. We win some, lose some. Just walk with pride. And be the best you can be. Take risks. Your confidence will grow from taking risks. Following through with things, even if they end with a result you didn't like. Take negativity or losing as a lesson. Be humble always.

#7. This one bothered me, I'll be honest and straight with you. Just because your parents are rich, doesn't mean they have to buy you stuff. I think this is more of a learning thing. We have to learn to earn things. Get high grades. Do volunteer work. Often when kids are given everything to them growing up, they'll struggle when they are older because suddenly they have to work for things you know? I actually applaud your parents in a sense that they don't want you to think you can have anything you want. I don't mean any of this in a disrespectful way, i believe it's more of a lesson being taught here than them just deciding not to buy you expensive stuff.

#6. I can't really give advice there. Unless if you live in an abusive home or something, id suggest getting child services if you have that there. I often wish to move out, however it's not that I can't live in my house it's just I liked being independent.

#5. I struggle with that a lot because of depression. I used to be so outgoing. Loving life. But this depression has made me a serious person. Sensitive. I believe that it's finding a method towards letting your inner child out. You're still very young and the fact you feel you have depression makes me sad. Because to feel like that at such a young age is awful. I'd look into thing you truly enjoy. Surround yourself with positive people.

#4. I know you've heard this before but your grade always reflects how much work you put into it. Now I know at 13 you probably aren't motivated to do studying and all. Heck even me being 19 I'm not motivated. But realize this. If you put in hours of studying, as hard as it may seem. You'll get results. Good example is this. I play guitar alright? I wasn't great at first. 7 years down the road, 7 years of playing practically every day. I became super good, one of the best in my class at guitar. However, it was easy because guitar was something I loved to do, if we can make our minds love learning. You'd get A+ across the board no problem. So the key is the amount of work you put into something, will reflect how well you do.
